text.p: Secretary of State Madeleine Albright approved on Thursday a visa for Gerry Adams, head of the Irish Republican Army's Sinn Fein political arm, because of the IRA's latest ceasefire, her spokesman said.
"The secretary did approve a visa request for Gerry Adams this morning," State Department spokesman Jamie Rubin told reporters.
Adams had been denied a U.S. visa for months when the IRA resumed its campaign of violence in Northern Ireland. But the group declared a new ceasefire last month, giving new life to peace efforts.
Asked if there were any restrictions on Adams' visa, Rubin said: "With regard to the restrictions on fund-raising, which is usually the question, there are none."
Adams applied for the visa on Aug. 11 in Dublin. But Rubin said he did not know when he would be coming to the United States or what he would be doing here.

Adams is deemed ineligible for entry into the United States because of what U.S. officials say was "his previous involvement in terrorist activities." As a result, he will always need a waiver of that ineligibility and a visa, which most Irish and British citizens do not need, to visit the United States, official say.
